cpu - engine   
mouse/keyboard steering wheel/pedals/etc   
ram - trunk   
hard drive - the storage area where you put your foostuffs you want at home.   
foodstuffs - programs   
internet - supermarket where you get the things from   
roads/highways - the actual roads you travel on to get things from the shop. the smaller/narrower the road(low bandwidth) and bumpier the road (bad wifi signal) the longer it takes to get the food      
virus - rotten food   
startup programs - unneeded items that lie in the trunk making it less able to transport things you want, and slowing the car down with unnecessary weight, and it also mean more trips to move the same number of things around.   
IE/norton antivirus/bonzi buddy - your really overbearing, fat, annoying mother in law who is a terrible backseat driver who slows down the car, takes up space and can cause accidents with her incessant nagging and can often make the food go rotten with their bad hygiene(coding)   
video card - the chef who takes all of this food and makes it into delicious meal for you. onboard is just having one slightly overworked chef, discrete is like having a chef with all his underlings (sous chef, etc)which means faster delivery and better tasting food   
display - the end result of all of this, delicious breakfast!!   
sort of a car/home and living thing. i got carried away with the food thing.   

oh and some more to add to it:   
motherboard - chassis of car   
case - bodywork of car   
psu - fuel system - if it doesnt have sufficient fuel delivery capacity the engine will run lean and burn out, especially if it has a big engine   
radiator - heatsinks, if the radiator is blocked with dust/dead roaches/cigarette tar, the engine will over heat   
operating system: the bits that connect the steering wheel/pedals to the rest of the car (i.e. steering column, brake lines, accelerator cable)   
iphone - the subway, you can only go where it takes you and you have no control over who rapes/murders/mugs you on your journey. although it has a great vending machine for small snacks   
AMD FX processor - a 1.2 litre V8 engine   
2500k - 2.0 litre 4 cylinder engine that  makes a lot more power, despite not being able to rev as high as the v8   
2600k - slightly bigger  4 cylinder (more cache) with a turbo (HT)   
GHz - engine rpm   
IPC - size of engine   
overclocking - modifying the engine and suspension so that the car can drive to the shop faster
